Threat Brief TB-2026-114 (TLP:CLEAR) - excerpt

Summary. Since 2026-10-02 the operators behind the "KettleLoader" campaign have exploited
CVE-2021-44228 (Log4Shell) and CVE-2023-4966 (Citrix Bleed) against exposed appliances running
firmware 13.1.49.15. Initial access (T1190) was followed by PowerShell execution (T1059.001) and
scheduled-task persistence (T1053.005). Spearphishing attachments (T1566.001) carried invoice.zip
and Statement_Oct.pdf lures.

Infrastructure. The first-stage downloader beaconed to hxxps://update-check[.]kettle-cdn[.]example[.]net/api/v2/ping
and to the raw address 198.51.100.23 on port 8443. A fallback panel lived at hxxp://203.0.113[.]77/panel/login.php.
Secondary domains: kettle-sync.example.org, files-kettle[.]example[.]com. The actors also kept a Tor
mirror at duckduckgogg42xjoc72x3sjasowoarfbgcmvfimaftt6twagswzczad[.]onion for victims.

Samples. The dropper (MD5 44d88612fea8a8f36de82e1278abb02f, SHA-1 3395856ce81f2b7382dee72602f798b642f14140,
SHA-256 275a021bbfb6489e54d471899f7db9d1663fc695ec2fe2a2c4538aabf651fd0f) unpacks a DLL compiled with
Visual Studio 14.29.30133 on 2026-09-30 11:42:07 UTC.

Monetisation. Ransom notes asked for payment to bc1qar0srrr7xfkvy5l643lydnw9re59gtzzwf5mdq or, for
USDT, the TRON wallet TR7NHqjeKQxGTCi8q8ZY4pL8otSzgjLj6t. An Ethereum address
0xde0B295669a9FD93d5F28D9Ec85E40f4cb697BAe appeared in one variant.

Detection notes. Hunt for the user agent string in proxy logs, the mutex Global\KTL_2026 and the
registry key HKCU\Software\Kettle. See also https://www.example.org/blog/kettleloader-analysis for a
second write-up.
